one_liner: Pixel entropy does not predict object-level failure: the granularity mismatch at the heart of segmentation uncertainty.
problem: Uncertainty is produced per-pixel but consumed per-object (is THIS lesion trustworthy?). Whether pixel-level uncertainty aggregates into valid object-level confidence has not been rigorously tested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: standard aggregations of pixel uncertainty (mean/max entropy over mask) predict object-level errors (misses, hallucinations, gross misshaping) only weakly (AUROC<0.7), because object failures are correlated-error events invisible to independent-pixel statistics - and object-level failure needs its own predictor trained on object-level outcomes.
why_important: Every clinical/industrial consumer needs object-level confidence; if the standard recipe is invalid, the field's uncertainty outputs are decorative.
why_possibly_novel: Granularity-mismatch quantification for segmentation uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On 3 datasets, compute pixel-aggregate vs learned object-level confidence, compare AUROC for object-failure prediction.
main_risk: Learned object-level predictors may overfit failure modes of specific models; test cross-model transfer.

one_liner: Calibration degrades before accuracy under distribution shift: miscalibration as an early-warning canary for silent segmentation failure.
problem: Deployed models fail silently under gradual shift (weather, sensor aging). If calibration metrics degrade earlier along shift gradients than accuracy does, they provide label-free advance warning - the lead-lag relationship is unmeasured for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: along parameterized shift ladders (fog density, noise level, geography), expected calibration error inflects at milder shift levels than mIoU does (a measurable lead), and the lead size is consistent enough to define actionable monitoring thresholds - calibration is the canary, not just a companion metric.
why_important: Label-free failure forecasting is the missing piece of deployment monitoring; a validated lead-lag law would be immediately adopted.
why_possibly_novel: Lead-lag analysis of calibration vs accuracy under graded shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate models along synthetic and natural shift ladders (ACDC severity levels), plot ECE and mIoU inflection points, quantify lead consistency.
main_risk: ECE estimation needs labels too; the deployment version must use proxy calibration signals (agreement-based), adding a validation step.

one_liner: Instance count, not pixel count, governs long-tail segmentation: disentangle the two supervision currencies.
problem: Rare-class performance is attributed to 'few pixels', but classes vary independently in instances-per-class and pixels-per-instance; which currency actually buys performance is confounded in natural datasets.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched total pixels, many-small-instances classes substantially outperform few-large-instances classes (instance diversity teaches shape/context variation that pixel volume cannot), with a measurable exchange rate - so long-tail interventions should target instance acquisition, not pixel acquisition.
why_important: Directly changes data-collection strategy for rare classes (many quick examples beat few thorough ones), a high-leverage economics result.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled pixel-vs-instance supervision disentanglement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Subsample LVIS classes into matched-pixel/varied-instance and matched-instance/varied-pixel grids, train and compare per-class outcomes.
main_risk: Class semantics confound (small-instance classes differ in kind); use within-class subsampling designs.

one_liner: Measure the labeling ROI of uncertainty-routed annotation: does model uncertainty actually direct human effort to where it pays?
problem: Uncertainty-guided active labeling is widely assumed beneficial, but for segmentation the regions models are uncertain about (boundaries, ambiguous textures) may be exactly where human labels are ALSO noisy - buying little.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: routing annotation to high-model-uncertainty regions yields lower marginal model improvement per annotation-hour than routing to high-DISAGREEMENT-between-models regions, because self-uncertainty concentrates on irreducibly ambiguous pixels while cross-model disagreement marks learnable errors - an economics experiment with a counter-intuitive predicted winner.
why_important: Annotation routing policies move real budgets; identifying the right routing signal has direct multiplicative value across the industry.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head routing-signal comparison measured in Dice-per-hour is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fixed-budget annotation simulation plus small real-annotator study comparing routing signals on a medical and a driving dataset.
main_risk: Results may depend on annotator skill and label noise model; report across annotator pools.

one_liner: Ensemble disagreement decomposes into boundary jitter vs semantic conflict, and only the second predicts real failure.
problem: Deep-ensemble disagreement for segmentation mixes two phenomena: small spatial jitter of agreed boundaries, and genuine semantic conflicts (different labels/regions). Treating them as one scalar wastes the signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: after registering member boundaries (factoring out sub-3px jitter), the residual semantic-conflict component predicts object-level errors and OOD inputs far better than raw disagreement, while the jitter component tracks stimulus edge blur - two useful signals recoverable from one ensemble by simple decomposition.
why_important: Upgrades the most common uncertainty tool for dense prediction at zero training cost, and explains why raw ensemble variance underperforms expectations.
why_possibly_novel: Jitter/conflict decomposition of segmentation ensembles is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Decompose disagreement for a 5-member ensemble on clean and shifted data, compare failure-prediction AUROC of components vs raw variance.
main_risk: Registration of member boundaries is nontrivial at large conflicts - exactly where it matters; needs robust matching.

one_liner: The abstention cliff: models never predict classes below a training-frequency threshold, and the threshold is predictable from loss geometry.
problem: Rare classes are not just less accurate - below some frequency, models predict them literally never (silent class death). The location and universality of this cliff is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class prediction frequency vs training frequency shows a sharp cliff (not smooth decline) at a threshold determined by the class's feature-space overlap with head classes, consistent across architectures - class death is a phase transition predictable from data statistics, and no amount of training-length increase revives dead classes.
why_important: Practitioners assume more training or mild reweighting recovers rare classes; a documented death threshold with a predictor would change how teams triage the long tail.
why_possibly_novel: Class-death phase-transition characterization for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Frequency-ladder subsampling of LVIS/ADE classes across seeds, map prediction-frequency cliffs, regress thresholds on feature-overlap measures.
main_risk: Cliff position may drift with loss/sampler choices used in practice; map across common configurations.

one_liner: Conformal inner-outer mask pairs: distribution-free coverage guarantees for segmentation, tested for usability where it matters.
problem: Conformal prediction offers guaranteed-coverage regions, which for masks naturally become nested inner (surely-object) and outer (possibly-object) contours - but whether achievable interval widths are narrow enough to be USEFUL in real tasks is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: conformalized inner/outer mask pairs achieve nominal coverage with width overheads small enough for radiotherapy-margin and robot-grasp use in most cases (median annulus width under 15% of object diameter), but widths blow up predictably on ambiguity-heavy classes - producing the first usability map of conformal segmentation.
why_important: Guarantees without usability are academic; a domain-by-domain width atlas tells practitioners where conformal methods are deployable today.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: conformal segmentation papers exist; the usability-atlas framing with task-anchored width thresholds is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement split-conformal masks on medical + driving datasets, tabulate coverage and width distributions against task-derived width budgets.
main_risk: Exchangeability violations under shift void guarantees; report shift sensitivity honestly.

one_liner: Anomaly-segmentation benchmarks are boundary detectors in disguise: SOTA methods flag object-background transitions, not anomalies.
problem: Road-anomaly benchmarks reward high anomaly scores on unusual objects; but if methods' scores concentrate on ALL boundaries (of normal objects too), leaderboard success may reflect boundary-affinity, not anomaly understanding.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for leading anomaly-segmentation methods, a large fraction of their positive signal lies within thin bands around object boundaries (normal or anomalous alike), and a boundary-band-excluded re-evaluation collapses the leaderboard while a simple interior-focused baseline climbs - current metrics conflate edge-awareness with anomaly detection.
why_important: Anomaly segmentation feeds safety cases in driving; knowing whether methods detect anomalies or just edges is not optional.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-band ablation audits of anomaly benchmarks are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-score public anomaly methods with boundary-band exclusion on SegmentMeIfYouCan-style data, quantify rank changes.
main_risk: Some anomaly signal legitimately lives at boundaries; interpret with both included/excluded views.

one_liner: Validate the aleatoric/epistemic decomposition against ground truth ambiguity: at boundaries, current methods conflate what they claim to separate.
problem: Methods claim to separate data uncertainty (aleatoric) from model uncertainty (epistemic), but both explode at boundaries, and no one validates the decomposition against measured stimulus ambiguity (annotator variance) and measured model ignorance (OOD-ness).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at object boundaries, reported aleatoric and epistemic maps correlate with each other far more than either correlates with its ground-truth referent (annotator variance for aleatoric, holdout-domain error for epistemic) - the decomposition largely fails exactly where uncertainty is largest, and honest evaluation requires referent-anchored validation.
why_important: The decomposition justifies real decisions (collect more data vs accept ambiguity); if it is invalid at boundaries, those decisions are misinformed.
why_possibly_novel: Referent-anchored validation of the decomposition for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-annotator datasets with OOD splits, correlate each uncertainty type with its referent at boundary vs interior pixels.
main_risk: Referents are imperfect proxies; triangulate with multiple referent definitions.

one_liner: Miscalibration direction flips between head and tail classes: one temperature cannot fix a structured, sign-changing bias.
problem: Segmentation calibration is usually addressed with global temperature scaling, implicitly assuming uniform miscalibration; class-conditional structure (overconfident on rare, underconfident on common, or the reverse) is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class calibration curves show a systematic sign flip along the frequency axis (head classes underconfident, tail classes overconfident, driven by loss dynamics and label noise asymmetries), so global temperature scaling worsens one end - and the flip point is predictable from class frequency and co-occurrence entropy.
why_important: A sign-changing bias makes the standard remedy actively harmful for part of the label space - important for any consumer of segmentation confidences.
why_possibly_novel: Frequency-resolved calibration-sign analysis for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute per-class reliability diagrams on ADE/LVIS models, locate sign structure, test global-vs-per-class temperature consequences.
main_risk: Per-class calibration estimates are noisy for the rarest classes; use hierarchical estimation.

one_liner: Are tumor-volume confidence intervals valid? Propagate segmentation uncertainty into derived clinical quantities and test empirical coverage.
problem: Downstream users consume derived scalars (volumes, diameters, areas) with error bars produced from pixel uncertainties under independence assumptions that boundary-correlated errors violate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: volume CIs computed under pixel-independence are anti-conservative by 2-5x (empirical coverage far below nominal) because boundary errors are long-range correlated, and correlation-aware propagation (sampling coherent boundary perturbations) restores near-nominal coverage without model changes - a purely statistical fix to a clinically dangerous underestimate.
why_important: Treatment monitoring uses volume changes; overconfident CIs can turn measurement noise into false progression/response calls.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage-validated propagation for segmentation-derived scalars is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-rater or synthetic-GT lesion data: compare nominal vs empirical coverage across propagation schemes and uncertainty methods.
main_risk: Requires trustworthy reference volumes; synthetic-lesion anchoring mitigates.

one_liner: Region-level selective prediction dominates image-level: reject the 5% of regions causing 50% of risk instead of whole images.
problem: Selective prediction for segmentation typically abstains per-image, discarding mostly-correct outputs; per-region abstention could retain value while excising risk, but its operating curves are unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: risk-coverage curves for region-level abstention strictly dominate image-level abstention by large margins across datasets (same risk at 3-5x higher coverage), and the optimal rejection granularity (region size) is predictable from the spatial autocorrelation of errors - a complete recipe for deployable selective segmentation.
why_important: Converts selective prediction from an academic exercise into a practical tool: most of the image is usually fine.
why_possibly_novel: Granularity-optimized selective segmentation with dominance quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build risk-coverage curves at multiple abstention granularities on medical + driving models, verify dominance and granularity predictor.
main_risk: Region abstention needs downstream handling protocols (what fills rejected holes) - application-specific.

one_liner: Do uncertainty overlays help or hypnotize? Measure over-reliance dynamics when clinicians see model confidence maps.
problem: Uncertainty visualization is assumed to improve human oversight, but confidence maps could induce automation bias (trusting confident-but-wrong regions MORE) - the behavioral effect is unmeasured for segmentation review.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: showing uncertainty overlays reduces human error-catch rates in high-confidence-but-wrong regions (attention is captured by flagged areas, unflagged errors get a pass) while improving catch rates in flagged areas - net effect on total misses can be NEGATIVE when model calibration is poor, making overlay deployment conditional on calibration quality.
why_important: A pre-deployment behavioral law (when overlays help vs harm) is needed before uncertainty visualization becomes standard in clinical tools.
why_possibly_novel: Automation-bias quantification for segmentation uncertainty display is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (automation bias in general is KNOWN in human factors).
minimal_experiment: Controlled review study: radiology trainees correct model masks with/without overlays where some errors are confident; measure catch rates by condition.
main_risk: Human-subject study logistics; effects may vary with expertise level (include as factor).

one_liner: Context prior vs class prior in the tail: rare classes fail because their contexts are rare, not because their appearance is unlearned.
problem: Rare-class failure is attributed to insufficient appearance examples, but rare classes also occupy rare contexts; the two deficits (appearance model vs context prior) have different remedies and are never separated.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pasting rare-class instances into common contexts recovers a large fraction of their segmentation accuracy (context prior dominates appearance deficit), while common classes pasted into rare contexts degrade sharply - most 'long-tail appearance learning' framing misattributes a context-prior problem, redirecting fixes toward context-decorrelated training.
why_important: Copy-paste augmentation works (KNOWN empirically); this explains WHY and predicts when it will not (appearance-limited classes), converting a trick into a diagnostic-driven method.
why_possibly_novel: Context/appearance deficit decomposition via bidirectional pasting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Bidirectional paste experiments on LVIS tail/head classes, decompose error recovery by manipulation direction.
main_risk: Pasting artifacts help models detect pasted objects; use high-quality harmonization and artifact controls.

one_liner: TTA-disagreement as epistemic proxy fails exactly under systematic shift: characterize the validity boundary of consistency-based uncertainty.
problem: Test-time-augmentation disagreement is a popular free uncertainty signal, but under systematic shift all augmented views are fooled identically, silencing the alarm precisely when needed - the validity envelope is unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: TTA-disagreement tracks error well under stochastic corruptions (noise, blur) but decouples under systematic shifts (new sensor, new geography) with near-zero failure-prediction power there - and the decoupling is detectable ONLINE via disagreement-distribution shape, giving a self-diagnosing uncertainty signal that knows when it is blind.
why_important: Prevents dangerous false confidence in the cheapest uncertainty method, and the self-diagnosis extension rescues its deployability.
why_possibly_novel: Validity-envelope mapping with online self-diagnosis for TTA uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Correlate TTA-disagreement with error across stochastic vs systematic shift suites; test distribution-shape detector for decoupling onset.
main_risk: The taxonomy stochastic-vs-systematic is fuzzy at edges; define operationally by augmentation-space coverage.

one_liner: Top-2 logit margin at each pixel is a free boundary-ambiguity map: validate it against annotator disagreement without any uncertainty machinery.
problem: Models already compute per-pixel class margins; whether this zero-cost signal matches human boundary ambiguity as well as expensive Bayesian machinery does has never been benchmarked head-to-head.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the top-2 margin map correlates with annotator disagreement maps nearly as strongly as deep ensembles do (within 10% of ensemble correlation) at 1/Nth the cost, but ONLY for in-distribution boundary ambiguity - establishing a practical uncertainty hierarchy: margins for boundaries, ensembles for OOD, nothing extra needed in between.
why_important: A validated cost-capability hierarchy stops teams from paying ensemble costs for boundary questions margins already answer.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head referent-anchored comparison of margin vs ensemble for boundary ambiguity is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-annotator data, correlate margin maps and ensemble maps with disagreement; stratify by in/out-of-distribution condition.
main_risk: Margins are miscalibrated per-class (see frequency sign-flip idea); may need per-class normalization to shine.

one_liner: Semantically-weighted confusion: wrong-but-adjacent (car-truck) vs wrong-and-absurd (car-sky) errors have identical metric cost but wildly different consequences - measure the absurdity distribution.
problem: Confusion severity is flat in all standard metrics. The distribution of error 'semantic distance' - and whether newer models err more reasonably - is unmeasured, though consumers care mostly about absurd errors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models with similar mIoU differ up to severalfold in absurd-error rates (semantic distance above safety thresholds), the absurdity rate is NOT monotonically improved by scale or recency (some new models err more absurdly), and absurdity-weighted rankings disagree with mIoU rankings enough to matter for safety-driven selection.
why_important: Safety cases hinge on worst-case severity, not average overlap; an absurdity metric with published model profiles fills a real selection gap.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic absurdity-distribution profiling of segmentation models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (hierarchical metrics exist but adoption-focused profiling of the model zoo does not, to my knowledge).
minimal_experiment: Define semantic distance via ontology + human severity ratings, profile 10 public models, compare rankings vs mIoU.
main_risk: Semantic distance definition is contestable; validate against human severity judgments.

one_liner: Near-duplicate training images create overconfidence pockets: data attribution for segmentation miscalibration.
problem: Web-scraped training sets contain near-duplicate clusters; models see some visual patterns many times, plausibly producing spatially-localized overconfidence unrelated to true reliability - a data-side cause of miscalibration nobody audits.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: test-image regions visually similar to high-duplication training clusters show systematically inflated confidence at equal accuracy (an overconfidence pocket signature), and deduplicated retraining flattens these pockets - a measurable causal path from data redundancy to calibration structure.
why_important: Connects dataset hygiene to trustworthiness (not just accuracy), giving calibration auditors a new data-side lever.
why_possibly_novel: Duplication-conditioned calibration analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cluster training data by similarity, map test-time confidence vs nearest-cluster duplication level, retrain deduplicated for the causal leg.
main_risk: Similarity-to-training measurement is itself model-dependent; use external embedding for neutrality.

one_liner: What hides in ignore regions? Benchmarks' void labels conceal systematic model failures that count in deployment.
problem: Evaluation protocols exclude 'void/ignore' pixels (ambiguous, boundary, unlabeled regions). Models are unconstrained there, and deployment consumes those predictions anyway - what models actually emit in ignored zones is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: within ignore regions, model predictions are strongly model-specific and often absurd (class flicker, impossible layouts), inter-model agreement collapses (revealing that supervision, not learning, was constraining them), and downstream metrics that consume full maps (planning, rendering) degrade measurably due to ignore-zone behavior invisible to benchmarks.
why_important: The gap between evaluated pixels and consumed pixels is a silent deployment liability; quantifying it forces protocol honesty.
why_possibly_novel: Ignore-region behavioral audit is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Extract ignore-region predictions from public models on Cityscapes/ADE, measure inter-model agreement and downstream-task sensitivity to those zones.
main_risk: No GT there by definition; evaluation must use consistency, plausibility, and downstream proxies.

one_liner: Sub-10-example classes are retrieval, not generalization: feature-space nearest-neighbor tests reveal the memorization regime of the extreme tail.
problem: Classes with a handful of training instances still show nonzero test performance; whether this reflects generalization or disguised memorization (matching near-identical training instances) determines whether extreme-tail scores mean anything.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for classes under ~10 training instances, test-set successes overwhelmingly occur on test instances with near-duplicate training matches (feature distance below a threshold), and success probability drops toward zero as match distance grows - extreme-tail performance is retrieval performance, and benchmark tails measure dataset redundancy rather than model capability.
why_important: Recalibrates every long-tail leaderboard's bottom decile and separates two capabilities (retrieval vs generalization) that current metrics blend.
why_possibly_novel: Match-distance-conditioned success analysis for tail segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For LVIS rare classes, compute per-test-instance nearest-training distances, plot success vs distance, compare against head-class curves.
main_risk: Feature space choice affects distance; replicate across embeddings.

one_liner: Uncertainty as the first sensor to fail: under gradual weather degradation, which uncertainty signal rises first, and does its order match accuracy decline?
problem: Multi-signal uncertainty stacks (entropy, margin, ensembles, TTA) are compared on static benchmarks, but deployment needs to know their ONSET ORDER under gradually worsening conditions - who warns first, who warns falsely.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: signals have a reproducible onset ordering along weather-degradation trajectories (e.g. ensemble disagreement first, entropy last), the ordering is stable across scenes but differs across shift types, and combining onset order with signal levels identifies the shift TYPE label-free - uncertainty dynamics carry diagnostic information that static levels discard.
why_important: Deployment monitoring needs early, interpretable alarms; onset-order fingerprints add a diagnosis capability to mere detection.
why_possibly_novel: Temporal onset-order analysis of uncertainty signals is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Drive models along graded weather ladders (synthetic + ACDC), record all signals, test ordering stability and shift-type classification.
main_risk: Graded natural weather data is limited; synthetic gradients must be validated against natural anchor points.

one_liner: Confidence dilutes with vocabulary size in open-vocabulary segmentation: a predictable law makes scores incomparable across vocabularies.
problem: Open-vocabulary models score each pixel against arbitrary user-supplied class lists; adding distractor classes necessarily redistributes probability mass, so confidence (and thresholded decisions) depend on vocabulary size - a structural effect nobody models or corrects.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel confidence for the true class decays with vocabulary size following a predictable law (driven by embedding-space crowding around the true class), decision flips under vocabulary growth concentrate on tail/ambiguous classes, and a crowding-aware confidence normalization restores vocabulary-invariant behavior - fixing silent incomparability across deployments.
why_important: Open-vocabulary models are deployed with wildly different class lists; vocabulary-dependent behavior means the same model+image gives different answers by list choice - users deserve a characterization and correction.
why_possibly_novel: Vocabulary-scaling laws for dense open-vocabulary confidence are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep vocabulary sizes with controlled distractor sampling on OV segmentation models, fit decay laws, test normalization for invariance.
main_risk: Distractor choice affects the law's parameters; characterize semantic-proximity dependence explicitly.

one_liner: Seed-churn maps: pixels that flip between training runs form a free, model-intrinsic ambiguity atlas that matches human disagreement.
problem: Retraining with different seeds flips predictions on specific pixels (churn). This intrinsic instability is treated as noise, but its spatial structure may encode exactly the stimulus ambiguity that expensive uncertainty methods try to estimate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pixelwise churn across 5-10 seeds correlates with human annotator disagreement as strongly as deep-ensemble variance does (they are near-duplicate signals), churn maps are stable dataset properties (transferable across architectures), and published per-method 'improvements' concentrate suspiciously on high-churn pixels - simultaneously offering a cheap ambiguity atlas and a benchmark-noise audit tool.
why_important: One artifact (churn atlas) serves three uses: free uncertainty referent, benchmark noise floor, and reproducibility diagnostics for claimed gains.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: churn is studied in classification; dense churn atlases with the benchmark-audit application are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train 10 seeds of 2 architectures on Cityscapes, build churn atlases, correlate with multi-annotator data, overlay published method deltas.
main_risk: Compute cost of multi-seed training (moderate); mitigated by using smaller proxy models if transfer holds.

one_liner: Rare-context hallucination: models paint plausible-but-absent stuff classes (water under bridges, sky through gaps) driven by context priors overpowering evidence.
problem: Segmentation errors are usually studied as misclassification of present things; systematic hallucination of ABSENT classes in strongly-suggestive contexts (context-completion errors) is unquantified for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in contexts statistically associated with a class (bridge implies water below), models predict the associated class at measurable rates even when it is verifiably absent, the hallucination rate scales with context-class association strength mined from training co-occurrence, and evidence-ablation shows these pixels rely on context, not appearance - dense prediction has a measurable prior-override failure mode analogous to LLM hallucination.
why_important: Establishes hallucination as a quantifiable dense-prediction phenomenon with a data-statistics predictor - relevant for safety and for understanding context integration generally.
why_possibly_novel: Context-completion hallucination quantification for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate context-strong/class-absent images (dry canals, drained pools, bridges over roads), measure per-model hallucination vs mined association strength.
main_risk: Verifying true absence needs careful curation; some cases are genuinely ambiguous from single views.

one_liner: The tail is where annotation noise lives: rare-class 'errors' are disproportionately label errors, making measured tail performance a lower bound with a computable correction.
problem: Rare classes are annotated by workers with less exposure and lower agreement; model 'failures' there may substantially be annotator failures, systematically understating true tail capability.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert re-audit of model-GT disagreements will show the label-fault rate rising steeply from head to tail classes (annotator unfamiliarity effect), and correcting evaluated labels compresses the head-tail performance gap substantially - part of the long-tail problem is a long-tail-of-annotation-quality problem, with different implied remedies.
why_important: If the tail gap is partly measurement artifact, expensive tail-focused training methods are being judged against corrupted references - the field should fix references before methods.
why_possibly_novel: Frequency-resolved label-error auditing for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (classification label-error work is KNOWN: Northcutt et al.).
minimal_experiment: Sample model-GT disagreements across frequency deciles on LVIS, expert-adjudicate 2k cases, fit fault-rate vs frequency, re-estimate corrected gaps.
main_risk: Expert adjudication is itself imperfect for genuinely ambiguous tail categories; use multi-expert panels.
